docs.title: Portal
docs.text:
Portal is a public web page that serves as the digital archive for the TEXTaiLES project. It is built as a Directus extension that connects the project database to a public-facing interface, enabling users to:

  • Browse and access all digitized cultural heritage artifacts
  • View 3D reconstructed models of artifacts using model-viewer
  • Learn detailed information about each digitized object
  • Access direct links to all TEXTaiLES tools
  • Log in as an admin user to edit annotations on artifacts through integrated tools

docs.title: Admin User
docs.text: Portal offers the ability to modify artifacts as an admin user.

docs.title: Admin Login
docs.text: The Portal includes admin login functionality for authorized users. Admin credentials are the same as Directus user accounts, providing seamless authentication between the public Portal and the backend system.

docs.title: Editing Artifacts
docs.text: Logging in as an admin enables users to edit annotations and manage content for artifacts in the Collections.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Browse to the desired artifact in the Collections tab
  2. Click the "Annotate with THOTH" button on the artifact page
  3. The system automatically redirects you to the artifact scene in THOTH annotator tool
  4. Make your edits and annotations
  5. All modifications are automatically saved to the database

This streamlined workflow allows authorized users to quickly access and edit artifact data without manual navigation or separate login processes.

docs.title: Public User
docs.text: Without login, every user can access the desired artifact from the Collections and explore its content freely.

docs.title: Public Access Features
docs.text:
Public users have full read-only access to the digital archive, enabling them to:

  • View high-quality 3D reconstructed models interactively using the 3D model-viewer
  • Access detailed metadata and historical information about each object retrieved from the database

docs.title: Browsing Experience
docs.text:
Public users can:

  1. Browse all use cases (archaeological collections)
  2. View previews of artifacts within each collection
  3. Select any artifact for a detailed view
  4. Interact with the 3D model using the viewer controls (rotate, zoom, pan)
  5. Read comprehensive information about the artifact's history, origin, material and more.

No authentication is required for viewing and exploring the archive, making the cultural heritage artifacts accessible to researchers, students, and the general public worldwide.

docs.title: Public Link
docs.text:
The public link that anyone can access is the following:

https://textailes.athenarc.gr/archive

docs.title: Authentication (Directus)
docs.text:
This chapter describes how each tool should authenticate users using Directus credentials.

We cover two runtime scenarios:

  1. Service environment (internal network / Docker): eg. Directus reachable as http://directus:8055.

  2. External environment (outside the service): Directus reachable via https://textailes.athenarc.gr

docs.title: Directus base URL (DIRECTUS_URL)
docs.text: Do not hardcode URLs in code. Use an environment variable.

docs.title: Service environment (internal)
docs.text:
Inside Docker / internal network, use the Directus service name, eg:

  • DIRECTUS_URL=http://directus:8055

docs.title: External environment (public)
docs.text:
Outside Docker, use the public host:

  • DIRECTUS_URL=https://textailes.athenarc.gr

docs.title: Step 1 — Login (get access token)
docs.text:
Send credentials to Directus:

Endpoint: POST {DIRECTUS_URL}/auth/login

Headers:

Content-Type: application/json

Request Body:

{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "secret"
}

Response (success):

{
  "data": {
    "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
    "expires": 900000,
    "refresh_token": "abc123..."
  }
}

docs.title: Step 2 — Handle successful authentication
docs.text:
If the response is successful (HTTP 200), the credentials are valid. The tool can then create its own session (example: login_user(user_instance)).

Optional: If your tool needs to make additional requests to Directus API, extract the access_token from the response and include it in subsequent requests:

Authorization: Bearer <access_token>

docs.title: Internal Environment Example
docs.text:
If you only need to verify credentials without making further Directus API calls:

import requests

DIRECTUS_URL = "http://directus:8055"

resp = requests.post(
    f"{DIRECTUS_URL}/auth/login",
    json={
        "email": username,
        "password": password
    },
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
)

if resp.ok:
    # Credentials are valid, create your own session
    login_user(user_instance)

docs.title: External Environment Example
docs.text:
import requests

DIRECTUS_URL = "https://textailes.athenarc.gr"

# Same authentication flow as internal service
resp = requests.post(
    f"{DIRECTUS_URL}/auth/login",
    json={
        "email": username,
        "password": password
    },
    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
)

if resp.ok:
    login_user(user_instance)

docs.title: Collections
docs.text: The Collections tab provides access to the complete digital archive of artifacts.

docs.title: Organization
docs.text: Digitized artifacts are organized into use cases, which represent different archaeological collections. This structure allows users to explore artifacts by their archaeological context and origin.

docs.title: Browsing Artifacts
docs.text: Users can access a use case to view a preview of all artifacts within that collection. From the preview gallery, users can select their desired object to access a detailed view.

docs.title: Home
docs.text: The Home page serves as the landing page for the Portal, providing visitors with an overview of the TEXTaiLES project and quick access to the main features of the digital archive.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Portal is organized into two main sections accessible from the navigation:

docs.title: Collections Tab
docs.text: The Collections tab provides access to the complete digital archive of artifacts.

docs.title: Toolbox Tab
docs.text: The Toolbox tab offers direct access to the TEXTaiLES suite of tools.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
The Portal currently features:

  • Digitized Artifacts: All objects from various archaeological collections
  • Use Cases: 8 documented use cases demonstrating archeological collections
  • Available Tools: 6 specialized tools for artifact analysis and annotation

Note: Statistics are updated regularly as new artifacts and tools are added to the archive.

docs.title: Toolbox
docs.text:
The Toolbox tab offers direct access to the TEXTaiLES suite of tools. This section includes:

  • Links to all available TEXTaiLES tools and applications
  • Documentation and resources for each tool
